chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Poverty does not enter a house in which is the name Muhammad, or Ahmad, or Ali, or al-Hasan, or al-Husayn, or Ja'far, or Talib, or Abd Allah, or Fatima from the women.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What names prevent poverty from entering a house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), linking the spiritual purity of the Ahl al-Bayt's names to tangible divine blessings, including protection from poverty. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that these names are not merely identifiers but vessels of barakah, reinforcing the concept of 'Isma' (infallibility/purity) extending to the lineage and its representation in daily life. The inclusion of both male and female names underscores the universal applicability of this blessing across the entire family of the Prophet.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The poverty does not enter a house in which is a name, Muhammad, or Ahmad, or Ali, or Al-Hassan, or Al-Husayn, or Ja’far, or Talib, or Abdullah, or Fatima from the women’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Bakr ibn Salih from Sulayman al-Ja‘fariy who has said the following: “I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Poverty does not enter a house wherein a person’s name is Muhammad or Ahmad or Ali or al-Hassan or al-Husayn or Ja‘far or Talib or ‘Abd Allah or Fatimah of the women.’”
